_comment: 难度自测 reading passages. The passage text is taken from the site's own articles (article + paragraph indexes); questions are original. 'anchor' must occur in the passage (build fails otherwise, so an edited article cannot silently break its questions). 'answer' is the index of the correct option; options are shuffled at runtime.

passages.anchor: This way of trading is called barter

questions.q: According to the text, how can people pay for things today?
options: With coins, notes, cards and even phones
Only with coins and notes
Only with cards
With rice and fish

questions.q: Why did people in the earliest times not need money?
options: Families made their own food and clothes
Everything in the shops was free
They lived in very large groups
They paid with their phones
Exchanging goods without using money
Saving money in a bank
Making new coins
Going fishing with a friend

passages.anchor: The stamp shows that you have paid

questions.q: What does the text say about paper letters today?
options: Millions of them still travel every day
Nobody sends them any more
They only travel inside one country
They are faster than phone messages

questions.q: Why do you put a stamp on the envelope?
options: To show that you have paid
To show the address
To make the envelope red
To close the envelope

questions.q: Where can you take your letter, according to the text?
options: To a red box in the street or a post office
Only to your friend's house
To a bank
To a phone shop

questions.q: What happens to the body clock during puberty?
options: It shifts so that sleepiness comes later
It stops working for a few years
It makes teenagers need much less sleep
It moves earlier, as in adults

questions.q: When would a typical teenager naturally wake up?
options: Around nine or ten in the morning
At about six o'clock
At eleven o'clock at night
At the same time as younger children

questions.q: Why does the writer mention other mammals?
options: To show that the change is natural, not just a habit
To compare teenagers with pets
To suggest that animals need more sleep
To argue that culture causes the change

questions.q: What does the writer say about the share of left-handed people?
options: It has stayed about the same throughout history
It has grown quickly in recent years
It is very different from culture to culture
It is close to one in two

questions.q: In most people, which side of the brain controls the right hand?
options: The left side
The right side
Both sides equally
Neither side

questions.q: "The connection is not simple" refers to the link between …
options: which hand people prefer and how their brain is organised
cave paintings and ancient tools
culture and history
parents and their children
That childhood as we understand it is a fairly modern idea
That children used to have more time to play
That schools invented childhood
That young people were treated the same in every period

questions.q: In this passage, "shielded" is closest in meaning to …
options: protected
excluded
trained
rewarded

questions.q: What is the function of the first two sentences?
options: They describe a common assumption that the writer then questions
They give historical evidence for the main argument
They criticise modern parents
They define the word "adulthood"

questions.q: How did many cities treat their rivers for much of the twentieth century?
options: Mainly as a convenient way to carry away waste and water
As attractions for tourists
As protected natural areas
As their main source of drinking water

questions.q: Why did tight control of rivers seem sensible at the time?
options: Rivers flooded, smelled and got in the way of building
Engineers had nothing else to build
Rivers were considered too beautiful to touch
The law required all rivers to be covered

questions.q: What does "a remarkable reversal" refer to?
options: Planners now trying to bring rivers back to life
Rivers starting to flow in the opposite direction
Factories moving back to the riverbanks
More roads being built over rivers
